rationale_evidence.anchor: AI and nondeterminism ... Extract(Document). Run 1: A_1. Run 2: A_2. The outputs may differ. Therefore the system cannot rely on LLM(Document) being deterministic. Instead we need to record LLMExecution=(model,version,prompt,context,input,output,time). Then the epistemic record remains reproducible
rationale_evidence.statement: Discovers LLM extraction is inherently nondeterministic (two runs may differ), requiring an LLMExecution=(model,version,prompt,context,input,output,time) record so the epistemic event remains reproducible even though the underlying AI process is not.

rationale_evidence.statement: Identifies a fourth threat: recomputing a derived assertion under a later rule version can produce a different result, requiring RuleVersion and ModelVersion be part of provenance — knowledge is derived under a computational context.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Fifth threat — changing ontology ... an assertion was interpreted using ontology version O_1. Later O_2 changes the meaning of an entity or relationship.
